mainTopic: Animals on שבת: going out with a מרדעת or אוכף, placing a מרדעת on a donkey, and the dispute between רב and שמואל about hanging a טרסקל (feeding basket).
overview: Our משנה said a donkey may go out on שבת with a מרדעת. שמואל adds that this is only allowed if the cloth was tied on from ערב שבת. A later משנה and a ברייתא both support him, and the ברייתא also brings a מחלוקת about going out with an אוכף. Then רב אסי בר נתן asks whether one may even put a מרדעת on a donkey on שבת, and רבי חייא בר רב אשי says yes. רבי זירא explains that this follows רב, who permits hanging a טרסקל (feeding basket) for the animal's pleasure, and so all the more a מרדעת, which prevents suffering. שמואל agrees about the מרדעת but forbids the טרסקל, and a ruling of רבי יוחנן from ארץ ישראל is shown to match שמואל on that point. The גמרא explains why a מרדעת differs from an אוכף: either the saddle can fall off by itself, or, according to רב פפא, warming a donkey meets a real need while cooling it does not. Finally, a ברייתא about foals with feeding baskets is used to challenge שמואל. The גמרא answers that it speaks of small foals, where the basket prevents pain, and a proof from its wording continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: שמואל's condition: the saddlecloth must be tied on from before שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the משנה's permission. A donkey may go out with a מרדעת only if it was tied on from ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: And this applies only where it was tied to it from ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by adding a condition to the משנה. A donkey may go out with its מרדעת only if the cloth was already tied on before שבת began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה simply said a donkey may go out with a מרדעת. שמואל narrows that permission to a case where the cloth was tied on from ערב שבת. If it was put on during שבת, the permission does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A saddlecloth or padding placed on a donkey, mainly to keep it warm
'And this is only when…', a formula that adds a condition

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מרדעת and אוכף. A מרדעת is a soft cloth that protects and warms the donkey. An אוכף is a real saddle used for carrying loads. The rules for them differ.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shmuel said:
And that is only where it was tied to it
from Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁקְּשׁוּרָה לוֹ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by qualifying the משנה's permission for a donkey with a מרדעת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A donkey may go out with a מרדעת only if it was tied on from ערב שבת.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a later משנה's wording supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the precise wording of a later משנה supports שמואל. That משנה forbids a donkey to go out with a מרדעת 'when it is not tied to it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Our משנה is also precise this way. It teaches: A donkey may not go out with a מרדעת when it is not tied to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings support for שמואל from the exact wording of a later משנה in this פרק. The next steps will explain how that wording proves שמואל's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה forbids going out with a מרדעת 'when it is not tied to it.' רב נחמן claims these words, read carefully, point to שמואל's condition. This step only quotes the source. The actual reasoning comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is also precise', meaning the exact wording supports the point
'For it teaches', which introduces the quoted source

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Our mishna is also precise in this way,
as it teaches:
A donkey may not go out with a saddlecloth
when it is not tied to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for שמואל's condition.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that the מרדעת must be tied on from ערב שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A later משנה: 'אין החמור יוצא במרדעת בזמן שאינה קשורה לו'.

steps.title: What case does 'not tied' mean? Not tied at all would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the later משנה means. It rejects the reading 'not tied at all,' because that would be too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it means not tied to it at all, that is obvious! It might fall off, and he will come to carry it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests what 'not tied' means in the later משנה. It rejects the simple meaning, 'not tied at all,' because that would be obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An untied cloth could easily slip off in the street. The owner might then pick it up and carry it in רשות הרבים, so of course it is forbidden. A משנה would not bother teaching something so obvious. So 'not tied' must mean something less obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the case?', a request to define the exact scenario
'If you say…', which introduces a possible reading
'It is obvious!', meaning it would not need to be taught
'He will come to carry it', a concern of carrying in רשות הרבים

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say it is not tied to it at all —
that is obvious,
lest it fall off of it
and he will come to carry it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְשׁוּרָה לוֹ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out רב נחמן's proof by defining 'not tied'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly does 'not tied to it' mean in the later משנה?

steps.title: So it means not tied from before שבת, which proves שמואל right
steps.stepSummary: 'Not tied' must mean it was not tied from ערב שבת. By inference, our משנה's permission applies when it was tied from ערב שבת. שמע מינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean it was not tied from ערב שבת? By inference, the first clause speaks of a case where it was tied to it from ערב שבת. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's proof. The later משנה must be forbidding a cloth that was not tied from before שבת, so our משנה must be permitting one that was tied from before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'not tied at all' is too obvious, 'not tied' must mean 'not tied from ערב שבת.' The opposite case is the one our משנה permits: a cloth tied from ערב שבת. That is exactly שמואל's condition, and the גמרא confirms it with שמע מינה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, is it not…?', which introduces the only remaining reading
The first clause; here, our earlier משנה

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's condition is proven from the wording of the משנה. A donkey may go out with a מרדעת only if it was tied on from ערב שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not
that it was not tied from Shabbat eve?
By inference, the first clause is
where it was tied to it from Shabbat eve.
Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְשׁוּרָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rejected reading from step 3 to reach the only reasonable reading, which proves step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's permission applies only when the מרדעת was tied from ערב שבת, as שמואל said.

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees: saddlecloth tied from before Shabbat is allowed, saddle is not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same as שמואל. It allows a מרדעת tied from ערב שבת, but forbids an אוכף even if it was tied from ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: A donkey may go out with a מרדעת when it was tied to it from ערב שבת. But it may not go out with an אוכף, even though it was tied to it from ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that states שמואל's condition outright. The ברייתא also adds a rule about the אוכף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly says what שמואל said, which is extra support for him. It then rules that an אוכף is forbidden even if it was tied on before שבת. Tying it early does not help, because a saddle is gear for carrying loads, not something worn for the donkey's own benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way', which introduces a supporting ברייתא
A saddle used for carrying loads

phrases.english: That was also taught in a baraita:
A donkey may go out with a saddlecloth
when it was tied to it from Shabbat eve,
but not with a saddle,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּשׁוּר לוֹ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: even though it was tied to it from Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that supports שמואל, after the proof from the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly requires tying from ערב שבת.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits the saddle too, with conditions
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits even an אוכף tied from ערב שבת. His conditions are that the belly strap is not tied and no strap is passed under the tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even with an אוכף, when it was tied to it from ערב שבת. But only if he does not tie the belly strap on it, and only if he does not pass a strap under its tail.
steps.whatsHappening: Still within the ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion about the אוכף. He allows it under certain conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, an אוכף tied from ערב שבת is acceptable, like the מרדעת. However, it must not be strapped down the way a saddle is prepared for a real load. Once those straps are added, it clearly looks like the donkey is carrying a burden.

keyTerms.meaning: A strap fastening the saddle around the donkey's belly
A strap passed under the animal's tail to secure a load

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic מחלוקת about the אוכף, and the next exchange relies on it. A saddle's link to carrying loads is what makes it different from a מרדעת.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even with a saddle
when it was tied to it from Shabbat eve,
provided that he does not tie the belly strap on it,
and provided that he does not pass for it
a strap under its tail.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף בָּאוּכָּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the first opinion's ban on the אוכף in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אוכף tied from ערב שבת is permitted, as long as the belly strap and tail strap are not fastened.

steps.title: May one put a saddlecloth on a donkey on שבת itself?
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי בר נתן asks רבי חייא בר רב אשי whether one may place a מרדעת on a donkey during שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי בר נתן asked רבי חייא בר רב אשי: May one place a מרדעת on a donkey on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Leaving going out aside, may one even put a מרדעת on a donkey during שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was going out into רשות הרבים. This question is about the act of putting the cloth on the donkey on שבת, for example to warm it inside the private domain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He asked of him', which introduces a question to a scholar

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not about going out into the street. It is about putting the cloth on the donkey on שבת, inside the private domain.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי בַּר נָתָן
phrases.english: Rav Asi bar Natan asked
of Rabbi Chiyya bar Rav Ashi:
What is the law regarding placing a saddlecloth
on a donkey on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי בַּר נָתָן מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from going out with a מרדעת to putting one on during שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it permitted to put a מרדעת on a donkey during שבת?

steps.title: Answer: it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר רב אשי answers that it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר רב אשי gives a short answer: one may put a מרדעת on a donkey on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מרדעת is for the donkey's own comfort and warmth, so placing it seems harmless. The next step will challenge this answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Placing a מרדעת on a donkey on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: Challenge: how is this different from a saddle?
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי בר נתן challenges him. Why should a מרדעת be different from an אוכף, which may not be handled this way on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But what is the difference between this and an אוכף?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי בר נתן attacks the answer by comparing the מרדעת to the אוכף. Placing an אוכף on a donkey on שבת is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a מרדעת and an אוכף are items placed on a donkey's back. If an אוכף may not be put on during שבת, why should a מרדעת be allowed? The question asks him to name a real difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the difference between this and…?', a challenge by comparison

phrases.english: He said to him:
But what is the difference between this and a saddle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר רב אשי's ruling that placing a מרדעת on שבת is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מרדעת seems similar to an אוכף. Since putting on an אוכף during שבת is not permitted, the מרדעת should be forbidden too.

steps.title: He was silent and gives no answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר רב אשי stays silent and gives no answer to the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר רב אשי does not answer. For now, the challenge stands without a reply. רבי זירא defends him in steps 12–14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His silence means he could not explain on the spot why a מרדעת differs from an אוכף. His ruling is left under doubt for the moment. רבי זירא defends him in steps 12–14, and steps 24–27 explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He was silent', meaning he had no answer

steps.confusionAlert: Silence here does not mean he agreed or took back his ruling. It only means he had no ready answer to the challenge.

phrases.english: He remained silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The challenge of step 9 is met with silence.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי חייא בר רב אשי gives no answer here. Steps 24–27 explain how a מרדעת differs from an אוכף.

steps.title: A ברייתא: you may not even remove a saddle by hand
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי בר נתן cites a ברייתא. One may not take an אוכף off a donkey by hand on שבת. If removing is forbidden, then placing one is obviously forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him from a ברייתא: A saddle that is on a donkey should not be moved by hand. Instead, one walks the animal back and forth in the courtyard and the saddle falls off by itself. Now, if you said no to removing it, is there any question about placing it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי בר נתן brings a formal source, a ברייתא, to back up his challenge against permitting things placed on an animal on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids handling an אוכף even to take it off, which helps the animal. He argues that putting it on is surely worse. He therefore assumes that רבי חייא's permission would logically extend to the אוכף, and that this source contradicts it.

keyTerms.meaning: A saddle, a heavy pack-saddle used for carrying loads
He may not move it (מוקצה-type handling)
Is it even necessary to say? (a 'surely' argument)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse אוכף (a heavy saddle) with מרדעת (a light cloth placed on the animal to keep it warm). The whole sugya depends on the difference between them.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
A saddle that is on a donkey —
he may not move it with his hand,
rather, he leads it back and forth in the courtyard
and it falls off on its own.
Now, regarding removing it, you said no;
is placing it even a question?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinforces the earlier challenge (step 9) with a formal ברייתא after רבי חייא בר רב אשי stayed silent.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר רב אשי's ruling that one may place things on a donkey on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר from the ברייתא: removing an אוכף by hand is forbidden, so placing one is certainly forbidden.

steps.title: רבי זירא: leave him, he follows his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רב אסי to drop the challenge. רבי חייא בר רב אשי is following the opinion of his teacher רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Leave him alone. He holds like his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא steps in to defend רבי חייא בר רב אשי. He says the ruling has a solid source, and he is setting up the quote from רב that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense is not a new argument. It points to an authority, רב, whom the ruling follows. The proof itself comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
Leave him; he holds like his teacher,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ברייתא challenge by attributing the ruling to רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא בר רב אשי's ruling seemed baseless and contradicted by the ברייתא about the אוכף.
steps.terutzMaskana: His ruling follows רב, who permits placing a מרדעת on an animal.

steps.title: רב permits a feeding basket, and all the more so a saddlecloth
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that one may hang a טרסקל (feeding basket) on an animal on שבת. By קל וחומר, a מרדעת is permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: One may hang a feeding basket on an animal on שבת, and by קל וחומר a saddlecloth is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the source behind רבי זירא's defense: רב's ruling about the feeding basket, which he extends to the מרדעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's direct ruling is about the טרסקל. The permission for the מרדעת is learned from it by a קל וחומר. This shows that the ruling in step 8 was about the מרדעת, not the אוכף, though the גמרא will still ask in step 24 why a מרדעת is different from an אוכף.

keyTerms.meaning: A feeding basket hung on an animal's neck
An 'all the more so' argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
A saddlecloth or blanket that keeps the animal warm

steps.confusionAlert: רב חייא בר אשי (a student of רב) reports רב's ruling. The 'teacher' that רבי זירא refers to is רב.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
One may hang a feeding basket on an animal on Shabbat,
and by a kal vachomer, a saddlecloth.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that רבי זירא's defense refers to.
steps.raayaObject: Permission to place a מרדעת on an animal on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling permitting a טרסקל, extended by קל וחומר

steps.title: Explaining the קל וחומר: pleasure versus suffering
steps.stepSummary: The basket only gives the animal pleasure and is still permitted. A saddlecloth prevents suffering, so it is surely permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there, where it is only for pleasure, it is permitted, then here, where it is to prevent suffering, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly how the קל וחומר works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The feeding basket saves the animal from bending down, which is only a comfort. The saddlecloth protects the animal from cold, which prevents real pain. Since even a comfort is permitted, preventing pain is surely permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: Just as there, where it is for pleasure, it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא דְּמִשּׁוּם צַעַר — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן.
phrases.english: here, where it is because of suffering — all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the קל וחומר stated in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preventing an animal's suffering is a stronger reason to permit than giving it pleasure.

steps.title: שמואל: saddlecloth permitted, feeding basket forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל agrees about the מרדעת but forbids the טרסקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A saddlecloth is permitted; a feeding basket is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's opposing view. He disagrees with רב about the feeding basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the bottom line for the מרדעת. They split only on the טרסקל. שמואל evidently does not treat mere comfort as enough to permit placing the basket, so he cannot build רב's קל וחומר. He permits the מרדעת on its own terms, because it prevents suffering.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: A saddlecloth is permitted;
a feeding basket — is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a dissent from רב regarding the טרסקל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מרדעת is permitted on שבת; a טרסקל is forbidden.

steps.title: רב's ruling is reported to שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף tells שמואל what רב ruled about the feeding basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף went and said רב's teaching before שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story line that sets up שמואל's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling is given here. It only brings רב's teaching to שמואל's attention so that he can respond.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef went
and said Rav's teaching before Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transitions to שמואל's direct reaction to רב's ruling.

steps.title: שמואל sharply rejects רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that if רב really said this, he knows nothing about the laws of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If אבא (רב) said this, he knows nothing at all about matters of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל strongly dismisses רב's permission to hang a feeding basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection targets רב's טרסקל ruling, and with it the קל וחומר built on that ruling. It does not reject the permission for the מרדעת, which שמואל himself holds.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: He said to him: If Abba said this,

phrases.aramaic: לָא יָדַע בְּמִילֵּי דְשַׁבְּתָא וְלָא כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: he knows nothing at all about matters of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל's response to the report in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב's permission for the טרסקל only; the מרדעת remains permitted
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In שמואל's view, hanging a feeding basket for mere comfort violates the laws of שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also permits a saddlecloth
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, רבי זירא hears from רבי בנימין בר יפת, in the name of רבי יוחנן, that one may place a מרדעת on a donkey on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי בנימין בר יפת sitting and saying in the name of רבי יוחנן: One may place a saddlecloth on a donkey on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support from ארץ ישראל: רבי יוחנן also permits the מרדעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the leading authority of ארץ ישראל agrees with רב and שמואל on the מרדעת. This strengthens the permission that started this discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up (to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
he found Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: who was sitting and saying in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין מַרְדַּעַת עַל גַּבֵּי חֲמוֹר בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: One may place a saddlecloth on a donkey on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling from ארץ ישראל that agrees about the מרדעת.
steps.raayaObject: Permission to place a מרדעת on a donkey on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן, via רבי בנימין בר יפת

steps.title: רבי זירא approves; שמואל taught the same in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא praises the ruling and notes that אריוך (שמואל) explained it the same way in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Well said. And אריוך explained it the same way in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא confirms the ruling. Both ארץ ישראל and בבל agree that a מרדעת is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its face, רבי זירא is endorsing the permission for the מרדעת and crediting it to אריוך in בבל. The next steps ask why he credits only אריוך, since רב also permits the מרדעת. They answer that his praise was really for an added line that forbids the טרסקל.
steps.whatToRemember: An אוכף may not be put on or taken off by hand on שבת. A מרדעת, which protects the animal from cold, is permitted according to everyone. רב and שמואל disagree only about the טרסקל feeding basket.
steps.confusionAlert: אריוך is not a new person. The גמרא identifies him as שמואל (step 21). As steps 22–23 explain, the praise points to שמואל's ban on the טרסקל, not only to the מרדעת.

phrases.english: He said to him: Well said,
and so did Aryokh explain it in Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Endorses רבי יוחנן's ruling and links it to שמואל's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא endorses the ruling from ארץ ישראל and links it to אריוך in בבל. Steps 20–23 clarify which part of the ruling he meant.

steps.title: Who is אריוך?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'אריוך' is whom רבי זירא mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is 'אריוך'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a simple identity question: who is the 'אריוך' that רבי זירא named in his praise?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רבי זירא said that אריוך explained the law the same way in בבל. 'אריוך' is a nickname, so the גמרא wants to know which אמורא it refers to before it moves on.

keyTerms.meaning: אריוך, a title of honor ('lion-king') used for a great Sage in בבל

phrases.english: 'Aryokh' — who is he?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a name used in רבי זירא's statement in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the Sage called אריוך.

steps.title: אריוך is שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אריוך is שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: אריוך is שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know that רבי זירא was crediting שמואל specifically. This sets up the next question: why credit only שמואל, if רב agrees about the מרדעת too?

phrases.english: It is Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the identity question of step 20.

steps.title: But רב also said the saddlecloth is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רב also permits the מרדעת, so why did רבי זירא credit only שמואל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב also say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: רב also permits putting a מרדעת on a donkey, so why would רבי זירא name only שמואל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 15, שמואל agreed with רב about the מרדעת. So on that point both of them hold the same thing. Crediting only שמואל seems strange unless something else in the ruling belongs only to שמואל.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav also say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבי זירא tied the ruling to שמואל alone.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's crediting of the ruling only to שמואל (אריוך).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב and שמואל agree that a מרדעת is permitted, so naming only שמואל makes no sense.

steps.title: The praise was for the ending that forbids the feeding basket
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא heard the ruling end with 'one may not hang a טרסקל on שבת.' That part matches only שמואל, so he credited שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he heard him finish with: 'But one may not hang a feeding basket on שבת.' About that he said: 'Well said, and אריוך explained it the same way in בבל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling רבי זירא heard had an extra ending forbidding the טרסקל. Since only שמואל forbids the טרסקל (רב allows it), רבי זירא credited שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל agree on the מרדעת but disagree on the טרסקל (steps 15–17). The ending of the ruling from ארץ ישראל matched שמואל's view, so רבי זירא's praise 'יישר' was really aimed at that ending. The גמרא repeats רבי זירא's words here to show which part of the ruling the praise referred to.

keyTerms.meaning: He was finishing it with (an added ending)
A feeding basket hung on an animal's head or neck

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא's 'יישר' was not praising the מרדעת part, since רב agrees with that. It was praising the line that forbids the טרסקל, which is only שמואל's view.

phrases.english: Rather, he heard him finishing it with:
'But one may not hang a feeding basket on Shabbat.'
He said to him: Well said,
and Aryokh explained it the same way in Babylonia.
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats רבי זירא's words to show they refer to the טרסקל ending.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the focus of the praise to a specific part of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא was praising the permission of the מרדעת, which רב also holds.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was praising the ban on the טרסקל, which only שמואל holds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ruling of רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל matches שמואל, and supports שמואל against רב on the טרסקל.

steps.title: Why is a saddlecloth different from a saddle?
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees the מרדעת is allowed. So why is the אוכף (saddle) treated more strictly?
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees a saddlecloth is allowed. How is it different from a saddle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that all agree a מרדעת may be put on the donkey, and asks why the אוכף is treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we allow the מרדעת because of the animal's discomfort, the same reason should allow taking off the אוכף. Yet the אוכף may not be handled that way. The גמרא wants to know what makes the two cases different.

keyTerms.meaning: A saddlecloth, a soft cloth put on a donkey to keep it warm

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone a saddlecloth is permitted;
how is it different from a saddle?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת מַרְדַּעַת מוּתָּר, מַאי שְׁנָא מֵאוּכָּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who holds the ruling to a contradiction between the מרדעת and the אוכף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The agreed permission to place a מרדעת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal's comfort should allow handling the אוכף too, yet it is forbidden.

steps.title: The saddle can fall off by itself
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the אוכף is different because it can slip off by itself, so there is no need to allow removing it by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the saddle might fall off on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the אוכף is different because it may fall off by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the אוכף, the animal's problem can solve itself, since the saddle can slide off on its own. So the רבנן did not need to allow handling it. With the מרדעת, the animal stays cold unless someone puts the cloth on.

phrases.english: It is different there, since it is possible that it will fall off by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by their facts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מרדעת and the אוכף should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אוכף can fall off by itself, so handling it is not needed.

steps.title: רב פפא: warming is needed, cooling is not
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different answer: the מרדעת is for warming, which the animal needs. Removing the אוכף is for cooling, which it does not need.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here it is to warm the animal, there it is to cool it. To warm it is allowed, because the animal suffers from cold. To cool it is not allowed, because the animal does not suffer from heat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a second way to explain the difference between the מרדעת and the אוכף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting on a מרדעת warms the animal, and a donkey really suffers from cold. Taking off the אוכף would only cool it, and a donkey does not suffer from heat. The rule follows the animal's real discomfort (צער), not the type of object.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here it is to warm it; there it is to cool it.
To warm it: it has discomfort (from the cold).
To cool it: it has no discomfort (from the heat).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כָּאן לְחַמְּמָהּ, כָּאן לְצַנְּנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 24, different from step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any comfort for the animal justifies handling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only real discomfort justifies it. Cold causes a donkey discomfort, heat does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that the permission is driven by צער בעלי חיים: the animal must actually be suffering.

steps.title: Folk saying: a donkey is cold even in summer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא supports his point with a popular saying: a donkey feels cold even in the heat of תמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what people say: 'A donkey is cold even in the season of תמוז.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב פפא's idea with a common saying about donkeys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a donkey feels cold even in midsummer, then heat is never its problem and cold always is. That confirms why warming it is allowed and cooling it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what people say (introduces a folk saying)

phrases.english: And this is what people say:

phrases.aramaic: חֲמָרָא אֲפִילּוּ בִּתְקוּפַת תַּמּוּז קָרִיר לַהּ.
phrases.english: A donkey, even in the season of Tammuz, is cold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's answer in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that a donkey suffers from cold but not from heat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying: 'A donkey is cold even in תמוז.'
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone allows the מרדעת. It differs from the אוכף either because the saddle can fall off by itself, or (רב פפא) because warming answers a real need and cooling does not.

steps.title: Objection from a list of things animals may not go out with
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge (מיתיבי) by quoting a ברייתא that lists items animals may not go out with on שבת, including foals with feeding baskets in the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: A horse may not go out with a fox's tail, or with the red strip between its eyes. A זב may not go out with his pouch. Goats may not go out with the pouch on their udders. A cow may not go out with the muzzle on its mouth. Foals may not go out into the public domain with the feeding baskets on their mouths. An animal may not go out with the shoe on its foot, or with an amulet, even a proven one. This is a way animals are treated more strictly than people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. The key line is that foals may not go out with feeding baskets 'into the public domain', and the actual argument from it will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids the טרסקל only when going out לרשות הרבים. That suggests that inside a private area, hanging a טרסקל would be allowed, which would contradict שמואל, who forbids hanging a טרסקל at all. The ברייתא also notes that a proven amulet is allowed for a person but not for an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A red strip of wool hung between a horse's eyes
A man with a certain bodily discharge that makes him impure
An amulet that has been proven to work

steps.confusionAlert: This step only quotes the source. The actual question against שמואל, based on the words 'into the public domain' about the feeding baskets, comes in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: לֹא יֵצֵא הַסּוּס בִּזְנַב שׁוּעָל,
phrases.english: They raised an objection: A horse may not go out with a fox's tail,
nor with the red strip that is between its eyes.
A zav may not go out with his pouch,
nor goats with the pouch that is on their udders,
nor a cow with the muzzle that is on its mouth,
nor foals with the feeding baskets that are on their mouths
into the public domain,
phrases.notes: Keep an eye on this detail; the גמרא is about to use it to challenge שמואל.

phrases.english: nor an animal with the shoe that is on its foot,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בַּקָּמֵיעַ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מוּמְחֶה
phrases.english: nor with an amulet, even though it is proven effective
— and this is a stricter rule for an animal than for a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the טרסקל dispute and brings a ברייתא to challenge the view that forbids it.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling (accepted in step 23) that one may not hang a טרסקל on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids foals with טרסקלין only when going out to רשות הרבים, which suggests that hanging one in a private area is allowed.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: what an animal may go out with
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the ברייתא from Step 28. An animal may go out with a bandage on a wound, splints on a break, and an afterbirth hanging from it. Its bell may be plugged so it can walk with it in the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an animal may go out with a bandage on a wound, with splints on a broken bone, and with the afterbirth hanging from it. One may plug the bell on its neck, and then it may walk with it in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא it started in Step 28. It now gives the list of things that ARE allowed. This is still setup; the actual challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first listed forbidden items, including foals with baskets in רשות הרבים. Now it lists allowed items, all of which treat an injury or a natural condition of the animal. The plugged bell may be worn only in a חצר, so it does not ring and look like the owner is taking it to market.

keyTerms.meaning: A bandage tied over a wound
Splints placed on a broken bone
A bell hung on an animal's neck

phrases.english: But it may go out with a bandage
that is on a wound,
and with splints that are on a broken bone,
and with the afterbirth hanging from it,
phrases.notes: Hanging out of the womb after giving birth

phrases.english: and one may plug the bell on its neck,
phrases.notes: Plugged so it will not ring

phrases.english: and it may walk with it in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל יוֹצֵא הוּא בָּאֶגֶד שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quotation that Step 28 opened with מיתיבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of שמואל (and the ruling from ארץ ישראל in step 23) that one may not hang a טרסקל on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only finishes quoting the source. The attack itself is drawn out in Step 30.

steps.title: The inference: foals with baskets are allowed in a חצר, apparently for pleasure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forbids foals with feeding baskets only in רשות הרבים. So in a חצר it is allowed. Doesn't this refer to big foals, where the basket is just for pleasure? That would contradict שמואל, who forbids hanging a טרסקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: 'nor foals with baskets at their mouths into the public domain.' Only into the public domain is it forbidden; in a courtyard it is fine. Isn't this talking about big foals, where the basket is for pleasure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא to make its challenge. It reads a hidden leniency into the line about foals and baskets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא forbids the baskets only in רשות הרבים, a חצר must be allowed. If these are big foals, which can eat from the ground easily, the basket is only for comfort (תענוג). That would support רב, who permits hanging a טרסקל for pleasure, and contradict שמואל, who forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In any case it teaches': it points to the one line that matters for the challenge
Feeding baskets hung by an animal's mouth
Pleasure or comfort, beyond real need

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'in a חצר it is allowed.' The גמרא infers it from the fact that only רשות הרבים is mentioned as forbidden.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
Nor foals with baskets
that are at their mouths, into the public domain.
It is into the public domain that they may not,
but in a courtyard, it is fine.
What, is it not talking about large ones
and for the sake of pleasure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in Steps 28 and 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling (endorsed in step 23) that one may not hang a טרסקל on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read precisely, the ברייתא allows baskets in a חצר. If this is about big foals, the basket is only for pleasure, and the ברייתא permits it, as רב holds. That contradicts שמואל, who forbids the טרסקל.

steps.title: Answer: small foals, to prevent pain
steps.stepSummary: No, the ברייתא means small foals. For them the basket prevents real pain, so it is a true need and not just pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about small foals, and the basket is there because of their pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא as talking about small foals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young foal has long legs and a short neck, so bending down to eat from the ground hurts. The basket relieves real pain (צער), so even שמואל would permit it, just as he permits the מרדעת. The ברייתא is therefore no proof that a basket hung only for pleasure is allowed, and שמואל's ban stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No': the standard opening for rejecting the questioner's reading

steps.whyThisMatters: This defends שמואל's position: on שבת one may hang something on an animal to relieve its צער, but according to שמואל not just for its תענוג (רב permits even that).

phrases.english: No, it is about small ones,
and it is because of pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 30 by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (small foals rather than large ones)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about big foals, so the basket is for pleasure, which would contradict שמואל's ban on the טרסקל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about small foals, where the basket relieves real pain. This is permitted even according to שמואל, who forbids a טרסקל only when it is for pleasure.

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show that the ברייתא's own wording proves it is about small foals. The proof continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also precise in the wording, since it teaches...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof from the ברייתא's wording that supports the answer it just gave. The actual quote comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase דַּיְקָא נָמֵי means the answer is not just a possible way out. The ברייתא's own words point to it. The next line will show which detail in the wording proves the case is small foals.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also precise': the wording itself supports this reading
'Since it teaches': introduces the supporting words from the source
An inference drawn from the exact wording of a source

phrases.english: This is also precise, as it teaches

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins supporting the answer of Step 31 from the ברייתא's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא refers to small foals, where the basket relieves pain
steps.raayaSupportSource: The precise wording of the same ברייתא (quoted on the next עמוד)
